key_insight: For bounded-degree max-Ek-LINSAT over any finite field, the paper shows NP-hardness of beating the random baseline by more than O(1/√D), and argues this scaling is the benchmark for quantum and classical approaches alike.
engineering_relevance: For decoded quantum interferometry and related optimization heuristics, the main design target is no longer the baseline value itself but the constant prefactor in the 1/√D advantage gap.
method: Extends bounded-degree approximation-hardness from Boolean max-XORSAT to max-Ek-LINSAT(q,r) over arbitrary finite fields.
Proves NP-hardness of exceeding r/q + O_{q,r}(1/√D) when each variable appears in at most D constraints.
Compares DQI with classical vs quantum decoders, identifying quantum decoding as necessary to match the hardness scaling.
evidence_signal: The abstract summarizes theoretical complexity results and a decoder-specific information-theoretic bound for DQI, rather than empirical benchmark data.
watch_item: The claimed DQI scaling depends on decoder choice and bounded-degree assumptions, so practical performance may fall short if classical decoding or non-regular instance structure is used.
paper_title: Approximability limits for bounded-degree max-LINSAT and implications for decoded quantum interferometry
